source.author: stat
source.text: longa retro series, trepidum si Martis operti agricolam infandis condentem proelia sulcis expediam penitusque sequar, quo carmine muris iusserit Amphion Tyrios accedere montes, unde graves irae cognata in moenia Baccho, quod saevae Iunonis opus, cui sumpserit arcus infelix Athamas, cur non expaverit ingens Ionium socio casura Palaemone mater, atque adeo iam nunc gemitus et prospera Cadmi praeteriisse sinam: limes mihi carminis esto Oedipodae confusa domus, quando Itala nondum signa nec Arctoos ausim spirare triumphos bisque iugo Rhenum, bis adactum legibus Histrum et coniurato deiectos vertice Dacos aut defensa prius vix pubescentibus annis bella Iovis teque, o Latiae decus addite famae, quem nova mature subeuntem exorsa parentis aeternum sibi Roma cupit, licet artior omnis limes agat stellas et te plaga lucida caeli, Pleiadum Boreaeque et hiulci fulminis expers, sollicitet, licet ignipedum frenator equorum ipse tuis alte radiantem crinibus arcum imprimat aut magni cedat tibi Iuppiter aequa parte poli, maneas hominum contentus habenis, undarum terraeque potens, et sidera dones.
source.text_original: longa retro series, trepidum si Martis operti / agricolam infandis condentem proelia sulcis / expediam penitusque sequar, quo carmine muris / iusserit Amphion Tyrios accedere montes, / unde graves irae cognata in moenia Baccho, / quod saevae Iunonis opus, cui sumpserit arcus / infelix Athamas, cur non expaverit ingens / Ionium socio casura Palaemone mater, / atque adeo iam nunc gemitus et prospera Cadmi / praeteriisse sinam: limes mihi carminis esto / Oedipodae confusa domus, quando Itala nondum / signa nec Arctoos ausim spirare triumphos / bisque iugo Rhenum, bis adactum legibus Histrum / et coniurato deiectos vertice Dacos / aut defensa prius vix pubescentibus annis / bella Iovis teque, o Latiae decus addite famae, / quem nova mature subeuntem exorsa parentis / aeternum sibi Roma cupit, licet artior omnis / limes agat stellas et te plaga lucida caeli, / Pleiadum Boreaeque et hiulci fulminis expers, / sollicitet, licet ignipedum frenator equorum / ipse tuis alte radiantem crinibus arcum / imprimat aut magni cedat tibi Iuppiter aequa / parte poli, maneas hominum contentus habenis, / undarum terraeque potens, et sidera dones.
source.text_english: A long chain lies behind; if I shall thoroughly unfold the anxious farmer of hidden Mars, who buries battles in unspeakable furrows, and follow him to the end—by what song Amphion ordered the Tyrian mountains to draw near to the walls, whence came the heavy wrath against the kindred city of Bacchus, the work of savage Juno, by whom unlucky Athamas took up the bow, why the great mother was not terrified when her son Palemon was to fall into the Ionian sea, and even now let me pass over the groans and successes of Cadmus: let the boundary of my song be the confused house of Oedipus. For I would not yet dare to breathe of Italian standards or of northern triumphs, nor of Rhine brought twice beneath the yoke, of Ister twice forced under laws, of the Dacians cast down from their mountaintop by a confederate force, or of the wars first defended while the boys were scarcely grown, nor of you, O glory added to Latin fame, whom Rome, newly begun by your father and already maturing, longs to have as her own forever; though every boundary presses harder and the bright region of heaven, free from Pleiades and Boreas and the yawning thunderbolt, summons you, though the bridler of fiery horses himself fixes his bow shining high in your hair, or mighty Jupiter yields to you an equal share of the sky, may you remain content with the reins of men, lord of sea and land, and bestow the stars.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti facta virum.
reuse.text_original: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis / stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna / fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti / fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit / Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, / eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, / sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti / facta virum.
reuse.text_english: Phoebus, give me guidance, if the chaste tripod of the Cumaean prophetess stands as a witness in my house, if the laurel grows green on a brow worthy of it; and you, whose fame is greater over the open sea, since Caledonian Ocean bore your sails after, in anger, it had first borne the Phrygian Iulii, rescue me from the peoples and from the earth that holds the clouds, holy father, and favor the ancient deeds of men, while I sing them in reverence.
